key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: ACUTE worsening over hours, often history of known hernia that was previously reducible. LOCATION: Groin (inguinal or femoral region), may have lower abdominal pain if bowel involved. DURATION: CONSTANT pain since hernia became irreducible. CHARACTER: SHARP, CONSTANT pain at hernia site, becomes SEVERE if strangulation occurs. AGGRAVATING: Standing, straining, coughing worsen pain. Cannot reduce (push back) the hernia. RELIEVING: Lying down may decrease discomfort slightly but hernia remains out. NOTHING fully relieves pain. TIMING: CONSTANT and progressively worsening if strangulation developing. SEVERITY: 6-9/10 if incarcerated, 9-10/10 if strangulated. ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: Tender, firm, non-reducible bulge in groin. Nausea, vomiting if bowel obstruction. Overlying skin erythema if strangulation. KEY POSITIVES: Irreducible groin mass, known hernia history, sudden change from reducible to irreducible. KEY NEGATIVES: Easily reducible bulge suggests simple hernia without incarceration.

red_flags: Overlying skin changes (red, dusky, necrotic) - strangulation, call 911
Severe pain with fever - infected/necrotic bowel
Vomiting with abdominal distension - bowel obstruction
Sudden relief of pain - possible bowel perforation, call 911
